 5 Things to Do   •   Dining   •   Music   •   Nightlife   •   Theatre   •   Events   •   Exploration   •   Calendar   •   Contests The Scene 5 Things to Do: Holiday Sip & Stroll at Brookfield Zoo, Christmas at Cantigny, Train Takeover in Wheaton
 November 18, 2026 at 8:30 am CST Expand Holiday Magic at Brookfield Zoo Chicago runs select nights through Jan. 3, 2027. (Photo by Brookfield Zoo Chicago)
 By 5 Things to Do in DuPage and Cook Counties Holiday Sip & Stroll (Brookfield): Brookfield Zoo Chicago’s Holiday Sip & Stroll is from 5:30-9 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20. Guests will enjoy holiday cheer, warm drinks and seasonal cocktails, as well as the first look at Holiday Magic before the main event opens to the public on Saturday. This is for adults 21 and over only. Click here for more information or to purchase tickets.
 Christmas at Cantigny (Wheaton): Christmas at Cantigny opens for the holiday season on Friday, Nov. 20. Check out the half-mile light show illuminated garden paths, 28-foot tree, festive cocktails and more. Click here for more information or to purchase tickets. 
 Train Takeover at the Museum (Wheaton): Bring the whole family to the DuPage County Historical Museum between 12:30 and 4 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21 for this train celebration. It’s National Model Railroad Month and the DuPage Society of Model Engineers will have a model on display. Other events include a train-themed scavenger hunt and train crafts. Click here for more information.
 Second City Nut-Cracking Holiday Revue (Aurora): The Second City’s Nut-Cracking Holiday Revue opens Friday, Nov. 20 and runs through Dec. 23 at the Copley Theatre in downtown Aurora. Tickets are $45. Visit paramountaurora.com for more information on showtimes or to purchase tickets.
 An Evening with Gary Sinise (Glen Ellyn): Award-winning actor and author Gary Sinise will be at the McAninch Arts Center on the College of DuPage campus at 6:30 p.m. Monday, Nov. 23 to celebrate the release of his new book “Graceful Warrior: The True Story of a Son, a Father, and a Family Who Carried Each Other Through.” All attendees receive a pre-signed copy of  t he book and proceeds benefit the West Suburban Foundation for Disabled Veterans and disabled veterans in the community. Click here for more information or to purchase tickets.
